articles.title: Wealthier children score higher on intelligence, but quality parenting levels the playing field
articles.summary: Children from higher-income families show greater fluid intelligence, a new study finds. However, researchers discovered that increased parental time and positive parenting can effectively bridge this developmental gap, especially for disadvantaged youth.

articles.title: The hidden architecture of forgotten first languages in the human brain
articles.summary: Even after being entirely forgotten, the tonal languages we hear during our first months of life permanently alter the physical wiring of our brains, according to new imaging research on international adoptees.

articles.title: Psilocybin combined with talk therapy shows potential for treating anorexia nervosa
articles.summary: Anorexia nervosa is notoriously difficult to treat, often resisting standard care. Now, a new pilot study suggests that psilocybin therapy, paired with psychological support, could safely help reduce eating disorder symptoms and boost the motivation to recover.

articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to slower memory and thinking growth
articles.summary: Teens who start using cannabis may experience slower growth in memory, attention, language, and processing speed. Their abilities often developed normally at first, then began leveling off while nonusers continued improving. THC appeared to be the most likely driver, especially for worsening memory.

articles.title: Does Google Search favor a liberal view on immigration?
articles.summary: A new study analyzing Google Search results in Sweden found an overall positive slant toward immigration, but the search engine's ranking algorithm consistently prioritized neutral, unpoliticized links at the top of the page.

articles.summary: People with antagonistic personality traits tend to report more problematic sexual urges, according to a recent study in Personality and Individual Differences. But these links are small, indicating that many other factors influence unhealthy sexual behaviors.

articles.title: How specific masculine ideals are linked to anxiety and depression in men
articles.summary: A survey of adult men reveals that strict adherence to certain traditional masculine ideals, like extreme self-reliance, is linked to an inability to process emotions, which corresponds to higher rates of anxiety and depression.

articles.title: Frequent cannabis users wake up with their “stress hormone” already elevated
articles.summary: Frequent cannabis users may wake up with unusually high levels of the stress hormone cortisol, suggesting their daily stress rhythms could be disrupted. Researchers say the finding raises questions about whether using cannabis for stress relief might, over time, interfere with the very system that helps the body handle stress.

articles.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
articles.summary: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat triggered striking changes across the brain and body, including shifts tied to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and natural pain relief. Participants also showed brain connectivity patterns resembling those associated with psychedelic experiences, suggesting that powerful altered states may be achievable without drugs.

articles.title: Stress can scramble your brain’s internal GPS, MRI study finds
articles.summary: Stress may literally scramble the brain’s internal GPS. Researchers found that cortisol, a hormone released during stress, made people significantly worse at navigating a virtual environment and disrupted the precise activity of grid cells, specialized brain cells that help us understand where we are in space. When landmarks were missing, this navigation system nearly stopped functioning, while another brain region appeared to step in and compensate.

articles.title: Psychology research suggests a common response to negative emotions is worse for you in certain countries
articles.summary: Ruminating on negative experiences is tied to lower daily well-being, but a new study indicates this association is stronger in the U.S. than in Japan. The findings provide evidence that our cultural background influences how we process emotions.

articles.title: Scientists tracked 12 people in Antarctica for 10 months—what happened could shape future Mars missions
articles.summary: A ten-month Antarctic experiment found that astronauts may struggle not only with loneliness but also with spending too much time around the same people. Frequent contact was linked to greater tension and mistrust, while the crew increasingly divided into cultural and language-based groups.

articles.summary: A recent meta-analysis indicates that the four most common forms of dementia feature distinct immune system responses. These biological differences occur independently of other health conditions and might eventually guide targeted treatments for cognitive decline.

articles.title: Green tea compound shows promise in protecting the brain from obesity-related damage
articles.summary: A compound found in green tea might protect the brain from memory loss and structural damage caused by obesity. New research shows the compound reduces inflammation and triggers a cellular recycling process that preserves brain volume.

articles.title: Foldable synthetic molecules could infiltrate and bust apart the toxic protein clumps causing Parkinson’s
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a synthetic molecule called SK-129 that blocks toxic protein clumps linked to Parkinson’s disease. In mice, the lab-designed molecule reduced disease symptoms by targeting flexible, previously "undruggable" proteins in the brain.

articles.title: Zapping the ear’s vagus nerve might boost motivation efficiency in severe depression
articles.summary: A new study suggests that delivering mild electrical pulses to the ear can help people with severe depression better judge when a task is worth the physical effort, reducing the amount of energy they waste on unrewarding choices.
